prompt.context_jp: 御園が去ったあとの応接室に、小原の低い声だけが残った。
prompt.prompt_jp: 小原の低い声だけ___残った。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits after 「だけ」 marking what exclusively remained.

feedback.correct_en: This narrates a new scene: of all possible things, only Kobara's voice remained — exhaustive/identifying が works with だけ.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would reframe his voice as the topic, losing the sense of 'only this and nothing else' remaining. を needs a transitive verb.

prompt.context_jp: フェリックスに袖にされた今、こはぜ屋を叩き潰す段取りは急がねばならない。
prompt.prompt_jp: フェリックス___袖にされた今、…
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking the agent that did the brushing off.

feedback.correct_en: In passive constructions, に marks the agent — Kobara was brushed off by Felix.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make Felix the subject of 袖にする, flipping the sentence. で would mark means or location, not an agent.

contrast_examples.en: I was scolded by the teacher.

prompt.context_jp: 同じ頃、宮沢たちは連日、都内の企業を回っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 同じ頃、宮沢たち___連日、都内の企業を回っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking Miyazawa and the others as the established topic switching scenes.

feedback.correct_en: 同じ頃 shifts the scene back to known characters (Miyazawa's group) — は re-establishes them as topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce them as new/unknown, but they are already central. を doesn't fit a subject role.

prompt.context_jp: 約1億の設備投資の壁が 新規取引への道を閉ざした
prompt.prompt_jp: 約1億の設備投資の壁___新規取引への道を閉ざした。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking the newly-revealed obstacle.

feedback.correct_en: The '100 million yen wall' is new information identifying what blocked the deal — が highlights it as the discovered cause.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would mark it as already-established topic, draining the dramatic reveal. に doesn't mark a subject.

contrast_examples.jp: 資金の壁が立ちはだかった。
contrast_examples.en: The funding wall stood in the way (new info).

prompt.context_jp: ツルガヘルメットでの商談のあと。
prompt.prompt_jp: 話___最初から最後まで手ごたえがあった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle framing 'the conversation' as the overall topic being evaluated.

feedback.correct_en: The narrator is commenting on the whole conversation as a known entity — は sets it as topic, with 手ごたえがあった as the comment.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce 'a conversation' as newly identified info, which clashes with the reflective summary tone.

prompt.context_jp: ふいに、宮沢の携帯が短く鳴った。
prompt.prompt_jp: ふいに、宮沢の携帯___短く鳴った。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle fitting a sudden event in the narrative.

feedback.correct_en: 'Suddenly, his phone rang' is an unexpected event — が presents it as new information breaking into the scene.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn the phone into a topic ('As for the phone, it rang'), losing the surprise of ふいに.

prompt.context_jp: 「茂木にＲⅡを勧めたのは 村野さんですよね」
prompt.prompt_jp: 茂木にＲⅡ___勧めたのは 村野さんですよね。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking the direct object (what was recommended).

feedback.correct_en: 勧める takes a direct object — を marks ＲⅡ as the thing recommended to Mogi.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make ＲⅡ a subject, which doesn't fit 勧める here. は would awkwardly topicalize it inside a cleft.

contrast_examples.en: I recommended a book to a friend.

prompt.context_jp: 大地の口から、一つの会社名が静かに落ちた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 大地の口から、一つの会社名___静かに落ちた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that introduces 'one company name' as a newly surfacing element.

feedback.correct_en: 一つの会社名 is indefinite and newly introduced — が spotlights it as fresh information emerging from Daichi's mouth.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would presume the name is already known to the reader; it isn't yet. を doesn't fit the intransitive 落ちた.

contrast_examples.jp: ある言葉が口から出た。

prompt.context_jp: 飯山が独学の過去を語る場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 俺___こいつを設計するのに 人生の半分ぐらい使っちまった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking '俺' as the topic of a reflective monologue.

feedback.correct_en: Iiyama is reflecting on his own life as the ongoing topic — は signals '(as for me,) I spent half my life...'
feedback.incorrect_en: が would sound like identifying who among several people did it, which doesn't match a personal confession.

prompt.context_jp: ちょうど、応接室の隅に置いた携帯が、震え始めた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 応接室の隅に置いた携帯___、震え始めた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle fitting a new event (the phone starting to vibrate).

feedback.correct_en: A sudden, newly-occurring event in the narrative — が marks the phone as the fresh subject of 震え始めた.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn the phone into an established topic, undermining the dramatic timing (ちょうど).

contrast_examples.jp: ちょうどその時、ドアが開いた。

prompt.context_jp: あけみが宮沢に静かに問いかける。
prompt.prompt_jp: 社長___どうしたいの？
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle Akemi uses to turn to Miyazawa as the topic of her question.

feedback.correct_en: She directs the question at the known addressee — は picks him out as topic: 'As for you, what do you want to do?'
feedback.incorrect_en: が would ask 'who wants to do what' as if identifying among many, which doesn't fit a direct, intimate question.

prompt.context_jp: 最初に口を開いたのは、意外にも家長だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 最初に口を開いた___、意外にも家長だった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for the cleft structure identifying who spoke first.

feedback.correct_en: 「〜のは…だった」 is a cleft: the known action (speaking first) becomes topic, with Ienaga identified as the one.
feedback.incorrect_en: のが would make the whole phrase function differently, as a subject noun phrase; it doesn't fit the Xだった predicate here.

contrast_examples.en: The one who raised a hand was me.

contrast_examples.jp: 手を挙げたのが見えた。

prompt.context_jp: 目の縁に光るものを、あけみは見逃さなかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 目の縁に光るものを、あけみ___見逃さなかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking Akemi as the topic of this observation.

feedback.correct_en: Akemi is already a central known figure; the narrator comments on what she, specifically, didn't miss — は as topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would newly introduce her as 'the one who didn't miss it' (identifying), but the scene flows from her perspective, so は fits.

contrast_examples.en: It was Akemi who saw it.

prompt.context_jp: ふと、事務所の入口で人の気配がした。
prompt.prompt_jp: ふと、事務所の入口で人の気配___した。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking the newly-sensed presence.

feedback.correct_en: 気配がする is a fixed pattern — が marks the sensation freshly perceived, matching the ふと ('all of a sudden') cue.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would strangely topicalize 人の気配, breaking the spontaneous perception. を doesn't combine with intransitive する here.

prompt.context_jp: 目の前を通り過ぎていく茂木の足元――そこには、まぎれもなく陸王があった。
prompt.prompt_jp: そこには、まぎれもなく陸王___あった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking the dramatic discovery of 陸王 at Mogi's feet.

feedback.correct_en: The Rikuoh is revealed as the surprise — が emphasizes its newly-discovered presence ('there, unmistakably, was Rikuoh').
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn it into topic ('As for the Rikuoh, it was there'), losing the dramatic reveal that drives the scene.

prompt.context_jp: 小原が御園に、宮沢が買収を拒んだと報告する場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「___を切られましてね」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word that completes the idiom meaning 'to be sharply refused / told off'.

feedback.correct_en: たんかを切る means to deliver a sharp retort or refusal — fits Miyazawa's defiant rejection.
feedback.incorrect_en: 息を切る means to be out of breath; 口を切る means to be the first to speak. Neither captures a sharp refusal.

contrast_examples.en: To speak sharply to the boss.

prompt.context_jp: フェリックスに袖にされた今、こはぜ屋を叩き潰す段取りは急がねばならない。
prompt.prompt_jp: フェリックスに___にされた今、…
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word that forms the idiom meaning 'to be brushed off / rejected'.

feedback.correct_en: 袖にする/される means to coldly reject or snub someone — exactly how Kobara feels after Misono walked out.
feedback.incorrect_en: 手にする means to obtain; 背にする means to put behind. Neither expresses the sense of being rejected.

contrast_examples.en: She gave me the cold shoulder.

prompt.context_jp: 小原が城戸に短く指示を出す場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 先日の件 早急に 社内の___を頼む。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the business term meaning 'to arrange support behind the scenes'.

feedback.correct_en: 根回し is the classic Japanese business practice of informally lining up internal support before a decision — exactly what Kobara wants.
feedback.incorrect_en: 手続き is procedural paperwork; 仕上げ is finishing touches. Neither captures political maneuvering.

contrast_examples.jp: 会議前に根回しをする。
contrast_examples.en: Line up support before the meeting.

contrast_examples.jp: 書類の手続きを済ます。

prompt.context_jp: 小原の指示に対する関口の返事。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the formal response meaning 'Understood, sir.'

feedback.correct_en: かしこまりました is the respectful acknowledgement from a subordinate to a superior — appropriate for Sekiguchi to Kobara.
feedback.incorrect_en: わかりました is polite but neutral; 知りました would sound off, suggesting 'I came to know.' Neither carries the deferential business tone.

contrast_examples.jp: かしこまりました、承ります。
contrast_examples.en: Understood, sir — I'll take care of it.

contrast_examples.jp: わかりました、やります。

prompt.context_jp: 「ホントの負けってのは 挑戦することをやめた時だ」
prompt.prompt_jp: ホントの負けってのは 挑戦することを___時だ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb meaning 'to quit / give up (an attempt)'.

feedback.correct_en: 挑戦することをやめる means to stop making the attempt. Miyazawa's point is that defeat = ceasing to try.
feedback.incorrect_en: 忘れた means 'forgot' — unrelated. 止めた (とめた) means to physically halt something; here やめた (quit, give up) is the correct nuance.

contrast_examples.en: To forget to make an effort.

prompt.context_jp: 家長が富島を励ます場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「おい ゲン あんたも腹___や」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word that completes the idiom meaning 'to steel oneself / make up one's mind'.

feedback.correct_en: 腹をくくる means to commit, to resolve oneself for whatever comes — perfect for the moment of collective resolve.
feedback.incorrect_en: 腹わり (to be open-hearted) and 腹立て (to be angry) exist as different expressions and don't fit this encouraging context.

prompt.context_jp: レースに復帰した途端 また ___を返したように 近づいてくる
prompt.prompt_jp: レースに復帰した途端 また ___を返したように 近づいてくる。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word that forms the idiom meaning 'to flip one's attitude completely'.

feedback.correct_en: 手のひらを返す is the set idiom for a sudden about-face in attitude — Mogi describes fair-weather supporters.
feedback.incorrect_en: 目を返す and 心を返す are not standard idioms with this meaning.

contrast_examples.jp: 手のひらを返して褒める。

prompt.context_jp: 「技術の差は 僅かでも 込められた思いは ___の差なんです」
prompt.prompt_jp: 込められた思いは ___の差なんです。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the four-character expression meaning 'a world of difference'.

feedback.correct_en: 雲泥の差 (lit. cloud-and-mud difference) is the fixed phrase for an enormous gap — fits Mogi's claim.
feedback.incorrect_en: 天地の差 exists colloquially but 雲泥の差 is the canonical set phrase here. 大小の差 just means 'size difference' and lacks the dramatic nuance.

contrast_examples.jp: 両者には雲泥の差がある。

prompt.context_jp: 宮沢があけみに応援遠征の費用について答える。
prompt.prompt_jp: 会社は こんな状況でも ___と これとは 話が別だ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word that completes the common phrase meaning 'that's one thing, this is another'.

feedback.correct_en: 「それとこれとは話が別」 is a fixed expression distinguishing two matters — the company's finances vs. supporting Mogi.
feedback.incorrect_en: これとこれ or あれとこれ don't match the standard pairing; the idiomatic form uses それ...これ.

contrast_examples.jp: それとこれとは話が別だ。
contrast_examples.en: That's one thing, this is another.

prompt.context_jp: 窓の外の情景描写。
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds more natural as literary narration?

choices.text: 窓の外の街並みは、二人の間に張り詰めた沈黙をよそに、静かに暮れかけている。
窓の外の街並みは静かに暮れかけている、二人の間に張り詰めた沈黙をよそに。

feedback.correct_en: Japanese literary prose places adverbial clauses before the main verb; option A follows that natural flow.
feedback.incorrect_en: Option B postposes the 〜をよそに clause after the predicate, mimicking English order — this feels awkward in written Japanese.

contrast_examples.jp: 周囲の喧騒をよそに、彼は本を読んでいた。
contrast_examples.en: Oblivious to the noise, he was reading.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼は本を読んでいた、周囲の喧騒をよそに。

prompt.context_jp: 御園が融資条件を提示する場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds more natural for a formal business offer?

choices.text: シルクレイ製造機の設備資金として3億融資します。
シルクレイ製造機の設備資金として3億貸してあげます。

feedback.correct_en: 融資します is the standard business verb for extending a loan — neutral and formal, fitting Misono's register.
feedback.incorrect_en: 貸してあげます sounds overly casual and condescending ('I'll lend it to you as a favor'), inappropriate in a corporate negotiation.

contrast_examples.en: We will loan you 300 million yen.

prompt.context_jp: 宮沢が社員に助けを乞う場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds more natural as an impassioned plea?

choices.text: どうか みんなの力を貸してほしい！
どうか みんなの力をあげてほしい！

feedback.correct_en: 力を貸す ('to lend one's strength / help') is the fixed collocation for asking for assistance.
feedback.incorrect_en: 力をあげる is not an idiomatic phrase meaning 'help' — it would literally mean 'give (someone) strength' and sounds off.

prompt.context_jp: 茂木が村野に陸王を辞退する場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds more natural when politely declining?

choices.text: 今の俺は この陸王を履くことはできません。
今の俺は この陸王を履くことはできないです。

feedback.correct_en: 〜ことはできません is the standard, measured polite negative — fits Mogi's heartfelt, respectful refusal.
feedback.incorrect_en: 〜ないです is grammatical but feels colloquial and less composed; in a solemn, formal moment, 〜ません flows better.

contrast_examples.jp: 行くことはできません。

prompt.context_jp: 城戸が独白する場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds more natural for 'if you believe and don't give up'?

choices.text: 信じて 諦めなきゃ あるかもしれねえな 奇跡ってやつがよ
信じて 諦めないなら 奇跡っていうものがあるかもしれない

feedback.correct_en: Option A matches Kido's gruff, masculine register with 〜なきゃ, ってやつ, 〜ねえな — natural in his voice.
feedback.incorrect_en: Option B is grammatically fine but sounds textbook-polite, out of character for a hard-nosed coach's inner monologue.

contrast_examples.jp: やらなければいけません。
